item.research_question: How can the large compositional space of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloys be mapped to identify optimal elemental fractions that simultaneously maximize kinetic energy dissipation while minimizing projectile penetration depth and residual velocity under high-velocity impact?
item.material_system: AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloys (HEAs) with atomic fractions: Fe [15%, 25%], Ni [15%, 25%], Co [15%, 25%], Cr [15%, 25%], Al [0–40%]
item.processing_route: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using LAMMPS with EAM/alloy force-field for HEA and Lennard-Jones for Au-HEA interface; 0.1 fs time-step; NPT ensemble equilibration at 300 K and 0 bar for 10 ps; NVE ensemble for impact; Gaussian Process (GP) machine learning model with Matern 2.5 kernel (scale 5.5) trained on 64 quasi-random Sobol samples; Multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) with population size 100, crossover rate 0.8, adaptive mutation.
item.test_conditions: Cylindrical gold projectiles (radius 28 Å, height 78 Å) impacting cylindrical AlCoCrFeNi target plates (radius 215 Å, thickness 60.52 Å) at impact velocities (Vi) ranging from 400 m/s to 1100 m/s; strain rates spanning 10⁻¹ to >10⁴ s⁻¹.
key_findings: Prediction error of the Gaussian Process models remains within ±10% for kinetic energy dissipation (ΔKE), penetration depth (δ), and residual velocity (Vr).
Increasing impact velocity from 400 to 1100 m/s results in a 49.4% increase in ΔKE, 35.3% increase in penetration depth (δ), and 12.46% increase in residual velocity (Vr).
Increasing atomic fractions of Fe, Co, and Cr leads to increased kinetic energy dissipation and penetration depth, whereas increasing Ni and Al concentrations decreases both.

The configuration with 25% Al and 0% Ni (Al25(FeCrCo)75Ni0) exhibits the highest transverse displacement (penetration depth) and highest kinetic energy dissipation, along with the lowest residual velocity.
The FCC to HCP lattice transition involves approximately 1% of atoms in equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi HEA, compared to 3.73% (29,979 atoms) in the Al25(FeCrCo)75Ni0 HEA.
The optimal solution from multi-objective genetic algorithm maximizes ΔKE while minimizing δ and Vr, with direct MD validation showing perfect agreement with ML-MOGA predictions.
Residual velocity shows a sharp decline specifically with increasing Al concentration, unlike other elements which show mild or positive correlations.
item.mechanism: Increased Al concentration and decreased Ni concentration enhance plastic deformation of the target plate, leading to greater transverse displacement (penetration depth) and higher kinetic energy dissipation; the FCC to HCP structural transition is more extensive in high-Al/low-Ni alloys, contributing to higher energy dissipation.
item.limitations: The study is limited to the AlCoCrFeNi system and does not experimentally validate the results; the computational framework relies on the accuracy of the EAM and Lennard-Jones force-fields and the assumption of single-phase FCC structure for the modeled compositions.
item.future_work: The proposed generic computational framework can be extended to other HEA systems and various multi-physical property demands with conflicting objectives and inherent simulation variabilities.
quotes: The data-driven analysis reveals that a lower concentration of Ni with a higher concentration of Al leads to higher dissipation of kinetic energy and lower residual velocity, but with higher penetration depth of the projectile.
The FCC to HCP transition is represented by roughly 1% (7763 atoms) of all atoms in equiatomic HEA. In the case of Al25(FeCrCo)75Ni0 HEA, however, this percentage climbs to 3.73% (29,979 atoms).
The computational framework proposed here is generic in nature, and it can be extended to other HEAs with a range of non-aligned multi-physical property demands.
